name: Amanayé
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.note: extinct; only old wordlists/ethnography; Juliao 2005 cited on Glottolog is on related Anambe, not Amanaye

sources.citation: Michael, Lev et al. 2015. A Bayesian phylogenetic classification of Tupí-Guaraní. LIAMES 15(2): 193-221.
sources.note: downloaded to check its per-language source list; Amanayé is not in the sample at all.

sources.citation: Jensen, Cheryl. 1999. Tupí-Guaraní. In Dixon & Aikhenvald (eds.), The Amazonian Languages, 125-163. CUP.
sources.note: Family-level only: 'Stress in the protolanguage, as in most of the descendent languages, occurred on the final syllable of the stem' (exceptions named: Chiriguano, subgroup 2, Wayampi, Asuriní of Tocantins). Amanayé is listed in the classification (subgroup 8) but nothing language-specific on its stress.

sources.citation: Instituto Socioambiental, Povos Indígenas no Brasil: 'Amanayé' (língua section); GEDAI/UFPA 'Língua Amanayé' (Neves 2013); pt.wikipedia 'Língua amanaié'; Biblioteca Digital Curt Nimuendajú lingua:amanaye; TuLaR/TuLeD 'Amanaye' entry; Glottolog aman1266
sources.note: None of these say anything about stress. ISA: language belongs to Tupí-Guaraní (Rodrigues 1984), 'Hoje em dia os Amanayé não usam mais a língua materna'; sources cited are Nimuendajú 1914 and Nimuendajú & Métraux 1948. TuLeD sources for Amanaye: Rodrigues 1985, Nimuendajú 1914.

sources.citation: Mistieri, Fernanda Regina. 2013. Acento em línguas Tupi-Guarani: uma análise comparada. MA thesis, UNESP Araraquara.
sources.note: Comparative TG stress thesis; Amanayé appears only in the Rodrigues 1985 and Rodrigues & Cabral 2002 classification tables (Quadro 1, Ramo V 'Ararandewára-Amanajé'); no stress data or analysis for Amanayé.

sources.citation: Solano, Eliete de Jesus Bararuá. 2009. Descrição gramatical da língua Araweté. PhD, UnB (and Alves 2008 MA UnB on Araweté phonology) — consulted for what Rodrigues & Cabral 2002 say about Amanajé.
sources.note: Report that Rodrigues & Cabral (2002) used 'os dados do Ararandewára publicados em Lange (1914) e os dados do Amanajé coletados por Jeferson Barbosa (2002)' to place Ararandewára-Amanajé in sub-branch V; the added criteria quoted are vowel changes and person-prefix morphology — nothing on stress for Amanayé.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú, Curt & Alfred Métraux. 1948. The Amanayé. In J. Steward (ed.), Handbook of South American Indians, vol. 3: 199-202. BAE Bulletin 143.
sources.note: Nothing; p. 199 only: 'On the Amanayé language there have been published only two small vocabularies, both in 1914: Lange's and Nimuendajú's. It is the most distinctive of the Tupí dialects of the He- group.'

sources.citation: Lange, Algot. 1914. The Lower Amazon. New York/London: G. P. Putnam's Sons. Appendix 'Vocabulary of the Ararandeuaras of the Moju River', pp. 445ff.
sources.note: Only a pronunciation key (p. 446): 'As the vowels in the Tupi language undergo changes of pronunciation depending upon their position in the word, I have accented these in order to make them easily understood' — the 'accents' are vowel-quality diacritics; no word-stress statement.

sources.citation: Nimuendajú-Unkel, Curt. 1914. Vocabularios da Lingua Geral do Brazil nos dialectos dos Manajé do Rio Ararandéua, Tembé do Rio Acará Pequeno e Turiwára do Rio Acará Grande, Est. do Pará. Zeitschrift für Ethnologie 46: 615-618.
sources.note: Nothing stated: a bare three-column comparative wordlist with no prose. Every Manajé form carries an acute accent mark, overwhelmingly on the final syllable (tatá 'fogo', jahý 'lua', kwarahý 'sol', pirá 'peixe', arapuhá 'veado', apotá 'quero', hepiré 'pelle'; a few non-final: mái 'mãe', kúi 'cuia', herypawamóia 'sogra') — implicit final-accent transcription only, not a statement.

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon D. & Ana Suelly A. C. Cabral. 2012. Tupían. In L. Campbell & V. Grondona (eds.), The Indigenous Languages of South America: A Comprehensive Guide, 495-574. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: English restatement of the 2002 internal classification with per-subgroup phonological properties; check whether anything is said about accent in subgroup V / Amanayé.
sources.venue: The Indigenous Languages of South America: A Comprehensive Guide

sources.citation: Barbosa, Jefferson Fernando. 2002. Contribuição ao conhecimento da língua Amanajé. Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal do Pará (Belém).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: The only modern linguistic description of Amanayé (Glottolog's sole descriptive ref); analyses Nimuendajú 1914 + Lange 1914 plus data Barbosa collected himself c. 2000-2002; if any source states where Amanayé stress falls (or how Nimuendajú's accent marks are to be read), it is this one. Not in RIUFPA; print copy at UFPA (PPGL/Biblioteca Central) — ask Ana Suelly Cabral's group (UnB/LALLI) or UFPA.
sources.venue: Dissertação de Mestrado, Universidade Federal do Pará (Belém)

sources.citation: Rodrigues, Aryon D. & Ana Suelly A. C. Cabral. 2002. Revendo a classificação interna da família Tupí-Guaraní. In A. S. A. C. Cabral & A. D. Rodrigues (orgs.), Línguas Indígenas Brasileiras: Fonologia, Gramática e História. Atas do I Encontro Internacional do GTLI da ANPOLL, Tomo I, 327-337. Belém: EDUFPA.

sources.note: Uses Barbosa's Amanajé data and Lange's Ararandewára data to define sub-branch V; lists phonological properties per branch and may mention accent placement (stress shift is a diagnostic elsewhere in their scheme). Would give a citable second-hand statement if Barbosa 2002 stays inaccessible.
